candidates.rationale: $close is silently overwritten with adj_close by the evaluator while $low/$high stay raw, so this range ratio mixes adjustment scales -- exactly the defect working-memory rule 5 flags for audit on this stochastic-range family. $open keeps all three price terms raw-consistent without changing the range-position idea.

The 21-day low and the 10-day return term sit on overlapping timescales, making the value and momentum legs redundant rather than complementary; this factor also sits at rho 0.780 against its nearest archive neighbor (rule 8's saturated EPS/price family). Widening the low-window to 63 days separates the two legs' horizons.

The lone 2012 sign flip (stability 0.93) coincides with a momentum-persistent year that would punish a short 10-day reversal bet. A 21-day window makes the return control less of a pure short-term-reversal wager and further diverges this factor from its rho-0.780 sibling (693246746bbdc073).
Same adjusted-$close-vs-raw-$high scale mix flagged this round for the two other price-distance expressions; $open restores scale consistency while preserving the drawdown-from-21-day-high idea.

CS_ZSCORE is unbounded and outlier-sensitive on a right-skewed dollar-volume cross-section; the sole negative year (2003) lines up with a volume-spiking junk rally that a Z-score would overweight. CS_RANK keeps the liquidity-penalty idea but is bounded and outlier-robust.

Both negative years (2009, 2010) fall in the immediate post-crisis window, when dollar-volume spiked heterogeneously across names; a 63-day average dilutes that transient spike's influence on the earnings-yield-times-liquidity ratio.

This is one of the two expressions working-memory rule 5 names for auditing the adjusted-close/raw-high mix. Fixing the scale mismatch (rather than the 3.8-day half-life, which the TS_RANK(dollar_volume) leg already addresses via rule 12's winning pairing) keeps the structure intact on a consistent price scale.

Turnover (0.314 one-way, charged 0.011 of fitness) is the largest cost drag of the ten. The same liquidity slot built with TS_MEAN in parent 992f173c32687afe turns over about 4x less, so the noisy order-statistic TS_RANK is the likely churn source; TS_MEAN keeps the liquidity-normalizer idea while smoothing it.

IC half-life of 3.7 days is the shortest of the ten -- the signal decays before it can be earned. Slowing the momentum control to a 63-day average should make the underlying driver, and hence the signal, persist longer.

Both negative years (2003, 2009) are recession aftermaths, when leverage changes reflect forced distress deleveraging rather than deliberate capital-structure decisions. Extending the delta window to a full year filters out that acute cyclical noise.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Read the diagnostics: a factor whose IC is positive in most years and negative in two has a regime problem, one with high turnover is paying costs it does not earn back, and one whose IC half-life is short is being asked to predict too far ahead. Change the component responsible for the specific weakness you name.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. Very short deltas (5-day) on slow-moving fundamentals (accrual_gap) scored among the weakest (|t| 0.55). Slow-moving fields need longer differencing windows to carry signal.
  2. Five of fifteen rejects duplicated 9 to 15 nodes of one already-archived stochastic-range / dollar-volume-range subtree. That lineage is saturated; branch into new structural forms instead of recombining it further.
  3. A bare field proposed next to its own rank transform ($roa vs RANK($roa)) is a near-guaranteed correlation reject (rho about 1.0). Changing only the wrapper around an already-archived field is not a new signal.
  4. One reject used plain RANK instead of CS_RANK on a 252-day roa mean. Verify cross-sectional operators are applied consistently so rejections reflect true signal quality, not an operator slip.
  5. CS_RANK($close - TS_MAX($high, 21)) and CS_RANK($close / (TS_MAX($high, 21) + 1e-8)) mix adjusted $close with raw $high, yet both were accepted this round with the 2nd and 3rd highest fitness (4.553, 4.780). Given the known adjusted-vs-raw scale mismatch, audit whether that mixing inflated their scores before trusting them further, and flag any new $close-vs-$open/$high/$low expression the same way.
  6. TS_DELTA of a fundamental (roe, leverage, asset_turnover, operating_margin, earnings_per_share) at 21-63 day windows failed the cheap screen three times (|t| 0.07-0.53). TS_DELTA($leverage, 126) paired with a level term (CS_RANK($roe)) passed at fitness 3.859: prefer 126+ day windows for fundamental deltas, and pair a delta with a level rather than two deltas together.
  7. $accrual_gap (coverage 0.872) and the 126-day delta of $operating_margin (coverage 0.882) both missed the 0.90 bar by a similar margin, pointing to sparse reporting for these fields in this universe. Deprioritize them until coverage improves at the data layer.
  8. 5 of 20 rejections were archive_subtree near-duplicates, and each was only a window tweak (21 to 42, 2 to 5) or an added multiplier on an already-archived tree, never a structural change. The earnings_per_share/close ratio subtree alone accounted for 2 of them; change the operator or feature, not just the window, near these trees.
  9. A mechanically similar feature or operator swap without structural change reads as a duplicate, not a diversification: $volume in place of $dollar_volume scored rho 0.850 against an existing member, and EMA in place of TS_MEAN at the same window scored rho 0.996. Pair any such substitution with a genuine structural change.
  10. Both crossover_not_a_fusion rejections used CS_RANK($roa), a 2-node wrapped-leaf archive member, as a parent; that size can never meet the fusion donation requirement. Exclude bare single-feature CS_RANK(feature) members from the fusion parent pool.
  11. 3 of 20 rejections were exact within-run duplicates: CS_RANK($roa) plus two high-low-range/dollar-volume normalization variants. De-duplicate the candidate pool before scoring, especially around that feature family.
  12. The round's top 3 fitness scores (5.128, 4.780, 4.553) all paired a fundamental level or a close-vs-high price-distance term with a volume-liquidity normalizer (CS_ZSCORE or TS_RANK of $dollar_volume). This pairing is outperforming pure return/fundamental combos; prioritize it next round.
